posts.html:
Practice two greetings and a reply in Modern Standard Arabic.

Start with marḥaban

مَرْحَبًا (marḥaban) means “hello.” Say it slowly once, then say it at a pace that feels natural. The ḥ represents a stronger breath sound than the English h.

Try a traditional greeting

السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ (as-salāmu ʿalaykum) means “peace be upon you.” A customary reply is وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ (wa ʿalaykumu s-salām), meaning “and peace be upon you.”

Practice both parts

Write the greeting on one card and the reply on another. Turn over the first card and try to answer before looking at the second.

posts.html:
Three phrases for keeping an English conversation going.

Ask for a repeat

Try “Could you say that again?” when you missed a complete sentence. If one part went by too quickly, try “Could you say the last part more slowly?”

Check what you heard

Repeat the key detail as a question. If someone says they arrive at fifteen past six, you can ask “Did you say six fifteen?”

Rehearse a short exchange

Ask a partner to give you a time or a street name. Request a repeat, confirm the detail, and thank them. Swap roles and try a new detail.

posts.html:
Build a short café exchange from a greeting, an order, and a thank-you.

Open with a greeting

Say “Bonjour” when you approach the counter during the day. Then try “Un café, s’il vous plaît” for a simple order.

Choose here or to go

You may hear “Sur place ou à emporter ?” A short answer works here. Say “Sur place, merci” to stay or “À emporter, merci” to take it away.

Change one detail

Practice the exchange again with “Un thé, s’il vous plaît.” Keep the greeting and reply the same so you can concentrate on the new word.

A small routine for fitting listening, recall, and speaking into your day.

Choose one useful phrase

Pick a phrase that fits a situation you might encounter this week. Read it, then listen to it if you have a recording.

Recall it without looking

Hide the phrase and say it aloud. Check it, then change one detail. For an introduction, try replacing the name or city.

Make the next session easy

Leave the phrase and its example where you will find them tomorrow. Begin the next session by recalling the same phrase before choosing another.

posts.html:
Use a short word to practice the direction and shape of Arabic script.

Find the first letter

In بَاب (bāb, “door”), start on the right with ب. The middle letter ا represents the long ā in this word.

Notice the connection

The initial ب joins to the following ا. The ا does not join to the letter after it, so the final ب is separated.

Say it and copy it

Say bāb, then copy it twice from right to left. Look for the dot below each ب when you compare your version with the model.

posts.html:
Practice a question you can reuse while finding your way around.

Learn one complete question

“Où est la gare, s’il vous plaît ?” means “Where is the train station, please?” Say it aloud as a full phrase.

Change the destination

Try “Où est la pharmacie ?” for the pharmacy or “Où est le musée ?” for the museum. Practice the article together with the place name.

Listen for a direction

Practice recognizing “à gauche” for left, “à droite” for right, and “tout droit” for straight ahead. Give a friend a destination and ask them to choose one of the three replies.
